# Opus 5 — ultracode

> An exceptionally well-engineered static Pokédex: ~32.7k lines across 146 TypeScript files with zero `any`, zero suppression comments and zero TODO markers, strict TS (plus noUnusedLocals/Parameters/verbatimModuleSyntax) gating the build, a pure-function domain layer (types, damage, stats, evolution, coverage, filtering) that never imports React, and a dependency-free build pipeline that resolves 638k learnset rows and 117k encounter rows into thousands of static shards with zero runtime API dependency. The core logic is reference-grade and independently verified: the type chart is the real veekun efficacy table (324 cells, 23 quirk assertions pass) with era-aware past overrides, the damage engine reproduces the cartridge's exact floor/pokeRound nesting and convolves the full 16-roll distribution for nHKO odds, the stat formulas handle both classic traps (Shedinja base-1 HP, nature applied after the floor), and evolution is a genuine recursive branching tree with cross-chain root resolution. Coverage is complete — 1025/1025 species reachable live with zero console errors. The adjudication sustained the auditor on all seven disputed features and both disputed axes, because the pattern is consistent: many surfaces are correct, complete, and exactly one step short of the top anchor (a tri-state type predicate with no counts or negation, a shiny flag threaded everywhere but with no shiny-specific surface and a toggle that does not reach the per-game tiles, per-Pokémon matchups that are defence-only and current-gen-only, favourites that cannot be starred from the browse grid, a keyboard layer that declares role="tablist" on 26 controls it never wires). Three findings are outright bugs rather than shallowness: alternate-form sprites are keyed off the wrong id space so non-default form rows silently render a different Pokémon; index-entry generation comes from the species row so generation filtering is wrong for all regional and Mega forms even though the builder reads the correct column elsewhere; and the landing page's primary search CTA throws an uncaught TypeError while 5 of the palette's 18 page results 404 against a stale hand-duplicated route table. Still the strongest submission in the field on engineering substance — the deductions are about the last mile, not the foundation.

## Strengths

- Domain logic is reference-grade: exact cartridge damage nesting with pokeRound and full 16-roll KO-chance convolution, correct HP/stat formulas with the Shedinja and nature-order traps handled, an 18-modifier ability layer that re-types the defence profile, and the real Gen V catch formula.
- Type effectiveness is derived from type_efficacy.csv rather than hand-written, verified complete (18×18, 324 cells) and correct on 23 quirk cases, with historically accurate past-override replay so a Gen I chart has no Fairy — and one shared implementation feeds all nine surfaces that need it.
- Zero runtime data API: the only client fetch is /data/*, backed by a documented positional-tuple wire contract, an in-flight-deduping cache with typed DataError, lazyWithRetry guarding the stale-shell chunk-404 white screen, and verified production cache headers plus HTMLRewriter OG injection on the shell.
- Typing and layering discipline: strict tsconfig gating the build, every specifier across 146 files resolving, src/lib never importing components/pages, builders importing only node:* plus the shared src/types/data.ts contract, 215 `///` doc comments and zero inline comments, and data-driven spec tables instead of switch ladders.
- Deliberate error handling that survives abuse: /pokemon/notarealpokemon renders a real NOT FOUND panel, garbage filter query state parses through allow-lists to '1,025 matching' instead of emptying, and the dex provider has an explicit failure screen with retry.

## Weaknesses

- Two wrong-data bugs visible in the live UI: builders/pokemon.ts:397 feeds a pokemon_forms.id into sprite paths keyed by pokemon.id (Unown-B renders deoxys-attack, and the fallback chain cannot fire because the wrong file exists at 200), and :296 takes generation from the species row so raichu-alola reports Generation I and the generation filter misfiles every regional/Mega form.
- The landing page's primary control is dead and throws: home/commandPalette.ts forges a ⌘K KeyboardEvent on `window` while AppShell.tsx:30-36 evaluates target.closest(...) first, so the hero search button and the 404 page's only button both emit an uncaught TypeError.
- Publicly reachable 500s in the worker: unguarded COLLECTIONS[segments[0]] prototype lookups (/api/constructor, /api/toString) and raw decodeURIComponent at :177 and :303 while safeDecode sits at :96 — /pokemon/%, a document route that should have served the SPA, hard-fails.
- Bounded but genuine rot against the 9 codeQuality anchor: a hand-duplicated route table that has already drifted (5 dead entries), divergent duplicate helpers (two generationRoman with different sentinels, three formatPercent with incompatible contracts, five ROMAN tables, three clamp), ~9 dead exports, SPECIES_TOTAL hardcoded in two pages, and a 687-line DamageCalculator default export.
- An ARIA contract announced and not implemented: ui/Controls.tsx Segmented declares role="tablist"/role="tab" in 26 places with no keyboard handling, and the mobile nav drawer lacks the Escape/trap/scroll-lock its own sibling FilterSheet implements.
- Service-worker hygiene: public/sw.js pins VERSION='pokedex-v1' with no build stamping while serving /data/* cacheFirst with no revalidation, so the activate-time purge can never fire and an installed client can serve last-deploy JSON indefinitely.

## Standout

The domain layer: a React-free src/lib that reproduces the cartridge damage formula floor-for-floor with pokeRound at each documented step and convolves the full 16-roll distribution into exact nHKO probabilities, sitting next to a type engine derived from veekun's efficacy CSV with descending-order past-override replay so the 18×18 matrix is historically correct per generation — one shared implementation feeding the detail page, compare, team analysis, coverage and the calculator alike.

## Vendored source

The source in this directory is the code the model wrote, copied verbatim from [its repo](https://github.com/guitaripod/pokedex-opus-5-ultracode) minus `node_modules`, build output, and generated data.

> 55 MB of PokéAPI data (public/data, 6032 files) and 41 MB of the upstream PokéAPI CSV dump (data-src, 180 files) stripped from the vendored source — it is data, not model-written code; regenerate with `npm run data` (the original repo keeps the CSV dump).

Canonical history and issues live in the [original repo](https://github.com/guitaripod/pokedex-opus-5-ultracode). This is a scored snapshot for the benchmark.
